newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia money, futures markets closed for holiday.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia money, futures markets closed for holiday.

text.p: The Malaysian interbank money market and interest rates futures market, the Malaysia Monetary Exchange, are closed on Thursday for a Moslem holiday. They reopen on Friday, July 18.
On Wednesday, interbank rates were steady as the market remained short of funds.
The overnight rate closed at 10 percent, after Bank Negara was heard lending overnight funds at 11 percent through an agent bank.
One-month money was at 10/12 percent against 9/10 percent on Tuesday, and one-week at 11/12 percent, against 13/15 percent.
Interest rate futures were mixed to reflect the uncertainty over the direction of interbank rates.
The three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was up one point to 92.38, or an implied yield of 7.62 percent.
The December contract was down one to 92.62, or 7.38 percent.
